---
title: "Input Data"
---

Both packages consume the same four kinds of input. This section
documents each one's expected schema, with worked examples drawn from
the [demo dataset](../demo-data/index.qmd) and code that uses the real
`masreml` / `masbayes` API.

| Input | In-memory shape | Companion file(s) | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SNP genotypes** | integer matrix $n \times p$, dosage 0/1/2 | `geno_G1.csv` + `snp_map.txt` | [SNP](snp.qmd) |
| **Microhaplotype calls** | integer matrix $n \times (2 \cdot n_{blocks})$ (compact) | `mh_genotypes/hap_geno_<chr>` + `microhaplotype_coordinates.csv` | [Microhaplotypes](microhaplotypes.qmd) |
| **Phenotypes** | data frame: `id`, fixed effects, response(s) | `pheno_continuous_G1.csv`, `pheno_binary_G1.csv` | [Phenotype](phenotype.qmd) |
| **Pedigree** | data frame: `id`, `sire`, `dam` | `d$pedigree` slot (no standalone file) | [Pedigree](pedigree.qmd) |

The fastest way to obtain all four pre-aligned is to load the bundled
canonical `.rds`:

```r
library(masreml)   # or masbayes — load_data() is byte-identical in both
d <- masreml::load_data("large")    # 200 individuals, 100 SNP, 50 MH blocks
str(d, max.level = 1)
```

`d$snp`, `d$mh`, `d$pheno`, `d$pedigree` are already aligned by
individual id; the four pages below describe each slot's schema and
common ways to construct it from your own data.
